source_evidence: Because many ETFs buy and sell portfolio securities in in-kind exchange (rather than for cash), they typically have fewer capital gains distributions – and thus lower taxes – than mutual funds.
question: Misconception: ETFs are tax-free because they are tax-efficient.
answer: ETFs are not necessarily tax-free. The source says many ETFs typically have fewer capital gains distributions—and thus lower taxes—than mutual funds. “Fewer” does not mean none, so tax efficiency should not be confused with being exempt from taxes.
